rationale: The Latin anchors *fragorem edere* (to make a crashing noise), *sonare* (to sound/resound), and *crepare* (to crack/burst) point to a violent, noisy breaking action — best captured by "hurl or thrust violently" (crash.v.10), which implies impact and the resultant loud noise. The Old English BERSTAN fundamentally means to burst/crash with sound, aligning with hurling/thrusting that produces a crash, rather than merely running quickly (dart.v.02) or simply breaking into pieces (smash.v.02).
